chunks: "Whoever performs the Hajj of Islam has untied a knot of the Fire from around his neck. And whoever performs two Hajj will remain in goodness until he dies. And whoever performs three consecutive Hajj, then performs Hajj afterward or does not perform Hajj, he is in the station of one devoted to Hajj."

key_terms.حَجَّةَ اَلْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required in Islam
key_terms.عُقْدَةً: a binding knot or tie, here indicating attachment to punishment
key_terms.مُتَوَالِيَةٍ: consecutive, one after another without interruption
key_terms.مُدْمِنِ اَلْحَجِّ: one constant and devoted in performing hajj

ai.seo_question: What are the virtues and spiritual rewards of performing hajj repeatedly in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the great merit of hajj and its lasting spiritual effects. It describes obligatory hajj as a means of deliverance from the Fire, presents repeated hajj as a source of ongoing goodness, and regards three consecutive pilgrimages as establishing the rank of one devoted to hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2205 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Whoever performs the Hajj of Islam has untied a knot of the Fire from around their neck. Whoever performs two Hajj will remain in goodness until they die. And whoever performs three consecutive Hajj, whether they perform another Hajj afterward or not, is regarded as one devoted to Hajj."
